title: VirtualBox Setup Check
transcript:
[user] FeatureName : Microsoft-Hyper-V-All DisplayName : Hyper-V Description : Provides services and management tools for creating and running virtual machines and their resources. RestartRequired : Possible State : Enabled CustomProperties :
[assistant] Here’s a **clean, no-fluff audit prompt** you can give Codex / Gemini / any CLI agent to verify your VirtualBox environment is fully enabled and optimized on Windows. --- ## 🔎 VIRTUALBOX FULL SYSTEM READINESS AUDIT PROMPT You are auditing a Windows 10/11 machine for full VirtualBox compatibility and performance readiness. Perform a complete verification and output PASS / FAIL for each section with exact command outputs. --- ### ✅ 1. CPU VIRTUALIZATION SUPPORT Check: - BIOS virtualization support (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) - Whether virtualization is enabled in firmware - SLAT support (EPT for Intel / RVI for AMD) Run: ```powershell systeminfo ``` Confirm: - "Virtualization Enabled In Firmware: Yes" - "Second Level Address Translation: Yes" Also run: ```powershell wmic cpu get Name,VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled ``` If Intel: Check VT-x If AMD: Check SVM mode Output: - CPU model - Virtualization support: YES/NO - SLAT: YES/NO --- ### ✅ 2. HYPER-V / VBS CONFLICT CHECK VirtualBox and Hyper-V conflict unless configured properly. Check: ```powershell bcdedit ``` Confirm: - hypervisorlaunchtype = Off Check Windows Features: ```powershell Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V-All ``` Also check: - Windows Hypervisor Platform - Virtual Machine Platform - Windows Sandbox - Core Isolation / Memory Integrity Output: - Hyper-V: ENABLED/DISABLED - VBS: ENABLED/DISABLED - Any conflict: YES/NO If enabled → flag as potential performance issue. --- ### ✅ 3. VIRTUALBOX VERSION + EXTENSION PACK Check: ```powershell VBoxManage --version ``` Verify: - Version installed - Extension Pack installed - Extension Pack version matches VirtualBox version Check: ```powersshell VBoxManage list extpacks ``` Output: - Version match: YES/NO --- ### ✅ 4. NETWORK DRIVER STATUS Check that: - VirtualBox NDIS6 Bridged Networking Driver is installed - VirtualBox Host-Only Ethernet Adapter exists Run: ```powershell Get-NetAdapter ``` Check Device Manager equivalent via: ```powershell pnputil /enum-drivers ``` Output: - Bridged driver installed: YES/NO - Host-only adapter present: YES/NO --- ### ✅ 5. GPU ACCELERATION STATUS Check: - GPU model - WDDM driver version - 3D Acceleration compatibility Run: ```powershell dxdiag ``` Confirm: - GPU driver model (WDDM 2.x+) - VRAM size Output: - GPU virtualization compatible: YES/NO --- ### ✅ 6. AVAILABLE RESOURCES Check: ```powershell wmic computersystem get TotalPhysicalMemory wmic cpu get NumberOfCores,NumberOfLogicalProcessors ``` Output: - RAM total - Logical cores - Recommended max VM RAM (50% rule) - Recommended max vCPUs (half logical cores) --- ### ✅ 7. TEST VM DRY RUN Create a temporary test VM: ```powershell VBoxManage createvm --name TEST_AUDIT --register VBoxManage modifyvm TEST_AUDIT --memory 2048 --cpus 2 --ioapic on --pae on --nestedpaging on VBoxManage startvm TEST_AUDIT --type headless ``` If it fails: Output exact error. Then delete: ```powershell VBoxManage unregistervm TEST_AUDIT --delete ``` --- ### ✅ 8. FINAL REPORT FORMAT Output: ``` VIRTUALBOX READINESS SCORE: X / 8 CPU Virtualization: PASS/FAIL Hyper-V Conflict: PASS/FAIL VirtualBox Install: PASS/FAIL Networking: PASS/FAIL GPU Support: PASS/FAIL System Resources: PASS/FAIL Test VM Launch: PASS/FAIL Overall Status: - READY - READY (Performance Limited) - NOT READY ``` --- If failures exist: Provide exact fix steps with commands. --- If you want, I can also give you: • A one-click PowerShell script that runs this entire audit automatically • A BIOS checklist specific to your CPU • A performance-optimized config for running Linux + Windows VMs side-by-side • Or a hardened setup guide if this is for NeuralOS / WinShadow integration Tell me which direction you're going.

[assistant] Good. That tells us exactly what’s happening. You have: ``` State : Enabled FeatureName : Microsoft-Hyper-V-All ``` That means **Hyper-V is fully active**. Now here’s the truth: If Hyper-V is enabled, VirtualBox does NOT run in true VT-x / AMD-V mode. It runs on top of Microsoft’s hypervisor (WHv mode). That results in: - Slower VM performance - Higher CPU overhead - Occasional weird networking issues - Nested virtualization limitations - Some 3D acceleration instability --- # 🔎 What This Means For You You have two possible configurations: ### OPTION A — Keep Hyper-V Enabled Use VirtualBox in compatibility mode. Good if: - You use WSL2 - You use Docker Desktop (WSL backend) - You use Windows Sandbox - You rely on VBS / Memory Integrity Performance: Moderate Stability: Fine Raw power: Reduced --- ### OPTION B — Disable Hyper-V (Recommended for max VirtualBox performance) If your goal is: - Full VT-x / AMD-V speed - Better GPU passthrough - Lower latency networking - Running heavier Linux VMs - Building OS-level systems (like your NeuralOS / WinShadow VM work) Then disable it. --- # 🔧 How To Fully Disable Hyper-V (Properly) ### 1️⃣ Turn off Windows features Run as Admin: ```powershell Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V-All Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName WindowsHypervisorPlatform Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux ``` Restart after. --- ### 2️⃣ Force Hypervisor OFF at boot level This is critical: ```powershell bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off ``` Restart again. --- ### 3️⃣ Verify After reboot: ```powershell systeminfo ``` You want to see: ``` A hypervisor has been detected: NO ``` --- # ⚠ Important If you disable Hyper-V: - WSL2 stops working - Docker Desktop (WSL backend) stops working - Windows Sandbox stops working - Memory Integrity may auto-disable --- # 🧠 Strategic Recommendation (Based on Your Build Work) Given you're building: - Custom OS layers - WinShadow - Kernel-level integrations - Deterministic environments You want raw hypervisor control. I would disable Hyper-V and let VirtualBox use direct hardware virtualization. That gives you: - Better VM timing precision - More stable nested setups - More predictable deterministic builds --- If you want, next I can: - Check if VBS / Memory Integrity is still silently enabled - Build you a dual-boot hypervisor toggle setup (Hyper-V ON profile / OFF profile) - Or optimize a VirtualBox config specifically for heavy Linux + Windows VM dev work Your move.
